identity.title: Two dependent state updates in a branch

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets a to 5 and b to 9. If a is greater than b, set a to a minus b and add 2 to b. Otherwise, set b to b minus a and add 1 to a. Print a and then print b.
content.source_code:
a = 5
b = 9
if a > b:
    a = a - b
    b = b + 2
else:
    b = b - a
    a = a + 1
print(a)
print(b)

identity.title: Arithmetic condition decides whether a second variable is reassigned before it is used

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets savings to 200 and cost to 120. If savings minus cost is greater than or equal to 100, subtract cost from savings and store it back. Otherwise, set cost to 50 and then subtract cost from savings and store it back. Print savings and then print cost.
content.source_code:

cost = 120
if savings - cost >= 100:
    savings = savings - cost
else:
    cost = 50
    savings = savings - cost
print(savings)
print(cost)

identity.title: Division in the condition

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets x to 6 and y to 2. If x divided by y is greater than or equal to 3, set y to y plus x, and then set x to x minus y. Otherwise, set x to 0. Print x and then print y.
content.source_code:
x = 6
y = 2
if x / y >= 3:
    y = y + x
    x = x - y
else:
    x = 0
print(x)
print(y)

identity.title: State updates inside an if/elif/else chain

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets level to 3 and xp to 250. If xp is greater than or equal to 300, add 2 to level and store it back. Else if xp is greater than or equal to 200, add 1 to level and subtract 200 from xp, storing both back. Otherwise, set xp to 0. Print level and then print xp.
content.source_code:
level = 3
xp = 250
if xp >= 300:
    level = level + 2
elif xp >= 200:
    level = level + 1
    xp = xp - 200
else:
    xp = 0
print(level)
print(xp)

identity.title: Swapping two values with a temporary variable inside a branch

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets a to 10 and b to 3. If a minus b is greater than 5, swap the values of a and b using a variable named temp (set temp to a, then set a to b, then set b to temp). Otherwise, add 1 to a and add 1 to b. Print a and then print b.
content.source_code:
a = 10
b = 3
if a - b > 5:
    temp = a
    a = b
    b = temp
else:
    a = a + 1
    b = b + 1
print(a)
print(b)

identity.title: Multiple sequential updates to one variable plus a string assignment within a branch

content.prompt: Write Python code that sets stock to 12 and order to 5. If stock minus order is greater than or equal to 10, subtract order from stock and store it back, then assign status the value 'OK'. Otherwise, subtract order from stock and store it back, then add 20 to stock and store it back, then assign status the value 'Restocked'. Print stock and then print status.
content.source_code:
stock = 12
order = 5
if stock - order >= 10:
    stock = stock - order
    status = 'OK'
else:
    stock = stock - order
    stock = stock + 20
    status = 'Restocked'
print(stock)
print(status)
